title: Deep Work Is Meaningful
coreMove: Choose depth as a way to make work more satisfying by giving attention to something worth shaping well.
sourcePressure: The source frame says deep work is intrinsically satisfying and supports a more meaningful work life.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says deep work is fulfilling because passion matters; the real point is that attention changes the felt quality of work.

exampleSpecs.domain: a forensic accountant reconstructing a missing payment trail
exampleSpecs.audience: a detail-oriented professional who has started to feel numb from routine reviews
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fraud case stays vague unless the pattern is found
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she stops skimming transactions, traces one vendor code line by line, and feels the work sharpen as the pattern appears
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a ledger export with one vendor code highlighted in pale green

exampleSpecs.domain: a luthier repairing a cracked cello bridge for a youth orchestra
exampleSpecs.audience: a craft worker choosing attention over throughput
exampleSpecs.stakes: the instrument buzzes during auditions if the bridge is rushed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he slows down to shave the bridge by sound and fit, not by job-ticket speed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cello bridge held against a bench light with a hairline crack visible

exampleSpecs.domain: a disaster-response mapper cleaning satellite imagery after a storm
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical volunteer tempted to see the task as tedious cleanup
exampleSpecs.stakes: rescue crews may miss blocked roads if the map stays noisy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares the blurred first pass with the cleaned road layer and sees how sustained attention turned noise into usable guidance
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a satellite tile mottled with cloud cover and red road segments

exampleSpecs.domain: a court clerk indexing sealed exhibits in a complex trial
exampleSpecs.audience: an administrative professional whose precise work rarely gets public credit
exampleSpecs.stakes: a mislabeled exhibit can derail a hearing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he notices the satisfaction is not applause but the clean fit between exhibit, docket entry, and judge's question
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sealed evidence envelopes lined up beside a docket terminal

exampleSpecs.domain: a marine mechanic diagnosing a ferry engine vibration
exampleSpecs.audience: a tradesperson whose day can become either rushed fixes or absorbed diagnosis
exampleSpecs.stakes: the ferry misses the morning commuter run if the vibration is patched badly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a failed quick fix, she listens through the second test cycle and identifies the mount problem by staying with the vibration
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a torque wrench resting on a steel deck beside a vibration log

exampleSpecs.domain: a speech-language pathologist designing one exercise for a stroke patient
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician whose meaning comes from exact fit, not broad sentiment
exampleSpecs.stakes: the patient gives up if the exercise is too easy or humiliatingly hard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she adjusts the exercise after watching one failed consonant and writes a version that meets the patient at the edge of ability
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a therapy card with three crossed-out consonant pairs

skillTargets: explain why depth can feel meaningful
distinguish intrinsic satisfaction from external praise
identify when attention changes the experience of work
evaluate whether a task can become meaningful through craft-level engagement

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one task you are tempted to rush and identify the single detail that would make it worth doing with full attention.
